subject: Post-demo: Ellipsia validation checklist & trial plan
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@ellipsia.ai>, Tom Bowers <tbowers@ellipsia.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Ellipsia validation checklist & trial plan

Thanks again for the demo this morning — great discussion. I wanted to capture the follow-ups and a compact validation plan so we have clear gates for the POC. Below is a proposed playbook; please review and tell us what needs to change.

Goal: validate Redwood as the production inference path for Ellipsia’s summarization pipeline. We’re proposing a 2-week sandbox trial with explicit pass/fail gates.

Core success criteria (proposed)
- Latency: Median response <= 220ms at 512-token requests (p95 <= 600ms)
- Throughput: sustained 40 QPS for 512-token batching (burst to 80 QPS acceptable)
- Cost: baseline token cost <= $0.0025 / input+output token (aim to show path to <$0.002 with batching / quantization)
- Quality: automated QA on a 1k-sample holdout — target F1 >= 0.91 on entity extraction and summary ROUGE-L delta <= 0.03 vs current model

Evaluation plan (high level)
1) Share sample workload (you provided a subset this afternoon) — we’ll run smoke tests in our sandbox (1–2 days)
2) Instrumentation and metrics: we’ll enable token-level cost, latency percentiles, and per-request quality tagging in the trial console
3) Load window: run two 2-hour steady-state windows (day 3 and day 7) to measure throughput and tail latency
4) Edge cases: run 2000 long-sequence (>1k token) jobs to exercise KV cache and memory paths
5) Readout: day 14 — summary workbook with pass/fail on the four gates above

Owners & next steps
- Commercial & contract: Ben Carter (ben@redwood.com) — will propose provisional pricing and commit level
- Onboarding & infra support: Monica Patel (monica@redwood.com) — will coordinate sandbox credentials and sample dataset ingestion
- Success metrics & readout: me (Aisha) — I’ll track KPIs and run the eval workbook

Attachments: redwood_trial_agenda.pdf (agenda + instrumentation checklist) — sample workload link here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Fq-example-drive-link

Ask: could you confirm the proposed gates or suggest modifications by EOD Friday (2027-05-21)? If that works, Ben will send a one-page confirmation and Monica will schedule a kickoff.

Thanks,
Aisha
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---

From: Tom Bowers <tbowers@ellipsia.ai>

Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 17:45:20 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Ellipsia validation checklist & trial plan

Aisha — this looks good, thanks for the clear plan. A couple clarifying points before we lock the gates: 

1) The 40 QPS target — is that per model endpoint or aggregate across the cluster? For our baseline we expect ~25 QPS per endpoint and plan to run across 2 endpoints in parallel (so aggregate ~50).
2) Latency numbers: are these measured client-side (round-trip) or at the inference service? We have some network variability so aligning measurement method matters.
3) For the quality baseline, we can share the annotated 1k holdout — I’m attaching a sanitized CSV of examples (ellipsia_sample_workload.csv). Does Redwood provide a built-in pipeline for batch evaluation (we prefer an automated report rather than manual scoring)?

Also — SOC2 evidence and data residency: our security team will ask for the standard SOC2 snapshot + data handling notes. We don’t need anything special for a sandbox, but call this out so Monica can prep.

On the sample dataset: attaching ellipsia_sample_workload.csv (sanitized).

Thanks,
Tom
Dir. of ML Engineering | Ellipsia Labs

Tom / Samira — appreciate the quick turn. Quick answers and a commercial note.

- QPS: we’ll treat targets as aggregate per-trial (so 40 QPS aggregate, supporting your 50 QPS burst across 2 endpoints). We’ll size the sandbox to show the sustained 40 QPS window.
- Latency: we’ll report both server-side inference percentiles and client-side end-to-end RTT. For the gate, we’ll use server-side med/p95, but include a client-side readout in the workbook.
- Evaluation tooling: Redwood’s trial console can run the batch evaluation you want — we’ll upload the CSV and produce a per-request quality report (F1/ROUGE metrics) and attach results to the readout doc.

Commercial / next steps:
- Provisional trial allowance: $15k trial credit covering the two-week sandbox runs (applied to usage). If POC passes, we’ll credit that against an initial 6-month reserved commit.
- Paperwork: I’ll send a 1-page SOW and a trial confirmation (DocuSign) today. Deal id: DEAL-2027-2457.

Monica — please schedule the kickoff for Mon May 24 or Tue May 25 (30–45m). Provide sandbox keys and a short onboarding runbook.

Tom — once we have your confirmation on the gates, I’ll fire the DocuSign and the team will get the sandbox bootstrapped.
